title: Give constructive learner feedback
description: Ground feedback in the supplied work.
accomplishes: Ground feedback in the supplied work. Identify one strength, one priority improvement and an actionable next step. Use respectful language, avoid unsupported personal inferences and do not replace teacher judgement in consequential assessment.
prompt:
Act as an instructional designer.

Task: Give constructive learner feedback.

Input context:
- WORK SAMPLE: [WORK SAMPLE]
- OBJECTIVE: [OBJECTIVE]
- RUBRIC: [RUBRIC]
- NEXT TASK: [NEXT TASK]

Ground feedback in the supplied work. Identify one strength, one priority improvement and an actionable next step. Use respectful language, avoid unsupported personal inferences and do not replace teacher judgement in consequential assessment.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Feedback pattern
“Your comparison identifies the two sources clearly. The conclusion needs a link to a specific passage. Choose one claim, cite its supporting section and explain the limitation.” Tie comments to actual work rather than assumed motivation. This is an illustrative feedback draft and does not assess an identifiable learner or establish a grade.
